To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) our system can segment nuclei with an AUC of 0.839, 2) this AUC increases to 0.838 when we incorporate spatial information, 3) this AUC is 0.748 if we disregard spatial information, and 4) our segmentation system is robust to color non-standardness.

(1) SCEM is a novel approach to incorporate spatial constraints into the EM framework; (2) SCEM is able to improve segmentation performance; (3) SCEM is robust with respect to the spatial smoothness parameter, which is an important consideration in real-world scenarios; and (4) SCEM improves the robustness of the segmentation system with respect to severe color nonstandardess.

(1) our novel SCEM framework can be used in a Bayesian color segmentation system for histological images to improve segmentation accuracy, and (2) our SCEM-based system outperforms the same system without SCEM on a dataset of gastrointestinal tissue.
